title: St Andrew (30 November)
hookLine: the first called, the one who brought his brother, near the start of Advent
tomorrow: Year three close: the story and the circle

lines: WHAT SEEK YE? COME AND SEE.
cards: "What seek ye?" In John's Gospel, in the King James words, Jesus turns round and asks it of two men who have been walking behind him.
Their teacher, John the Baptist, had just pointed at him and said, "Behold the Lamb of God!" So they followed. They don't have a clever answer.
They ask where he's staying. He says, "Come and see." And they spend the rest of that day with him.
John's Gospel names one of the two: Andrew. And the next thing Andrew does is go and look for his brother. The church keeps his day on the thirtieth of November, near the start of Advent.

teach.h: HE FIRST FINDETH HIS OWN BROTHER.
teach.b: Then, John says, "He first findeth his own brother Simon, and saith unto him, We have found the Messias, which is, being interpreted, the Christ. And he brought him to Jesus." First findeth.
Before anything else, he gets his brother. Jesus is about to give that brother a new name: Cephas, a stone. We know him as Peter.
And John calls Andrew simply Simon Peter's brother. In the Orthodox tradition he is the First-Called: in John's telling, he follows Jesus before Peter arrives. Watch what he keeps doing.
A huge crowd on a hillside, nothing to eat, the disciples worried.
It's Andrew who notices a boy: "There is a lad here, which hath five barley loaves, and two small fishes: but what are they among so many?" He doesn't solve the problem.
He just brings the boy, and the little he has, to Jesus.
Later, in Jerusalem, some Greeks come asking to see Jesus. They ask Philip. Philip tells Andrew, and Andrew and Philip go and tell Jesus.
A brother, a boy, a group of strangers: each time, Andrew is bringing someone. There John's story of him ends.

teach.h: A CROSS SHAPED LIKE AN X.
teach.b: Tradition says he traveled far to preach and died on a cross shaped like an X, and that cross now sits on the flag of Scotland, where he's the patron saint.
His day near the start of Advent fits him: the season of waiting opens with the man who said, we have found him, and went to get someone else.

how: Churches that keep saints' days remember Andrew on the thirtieth of November, and in Scotland, where he is patron saint, the day is also kept as a national celebration.

games.q: you're Andrew. you've just spent a whole day with Jesus, and you think he's the one. what do you do next?
o: keep it quiet until you're sure.
go and find your brother, and bring him.
go back and report to John the Baptist.
games.why: he first findeth his own brother Simon: we have found the Messias. and he brought him to Jesus.

practice: Think of one good thing you've found, a walk, a choir, a quiet church, a book, a kitchen table where people are kind, and then of one person who might need it: not the easiest to ask, but the one who came to mind first.
Picture yourself asking plainly, with the words Andrew first heard: come and see. If you pray, pray for that person by name; if you don't, just hold them in mind.
